contribution: Developing the New Keynesian framework for monetary policy analysis, combining nominal rigidities with dynamic optimizing behavior to explain how central banks affect inflation and real activity
rationale: This is a best guess, not a confident forecast. The 2024 and 2025 prizes went to institutions and to innovation-driven growth, so a return to macroeconomics or monetary theory seems plausible. Woodford, Galí and Gertler perennially top citation-based predictions. Their framework underpins modern central bank models and inflation-targeting practice, and the post-2021 inflation episode has renewed its relevance. Gertler was left out of the 2022 banking-and-crises prize despite close links to Bernanke's work.
